editing: Project slides and actual recordings of the successful Vultr import check, AI investigation and AI recovery. Downloads were separately recorded from the same completed recovery workspace. Recorded movements are slowed to fit narration. The containment segment renders an actual completed fixed-program test. No additional model call was made for editing or verification.

scenes.name: problem
scenes.text: Shopify has already documented this problem: an import cannot be canceled once it starts, and included blank fields can overwrite existing values. Rewind helps you check the next import before it runs, and undo exact damaged values after a mistake while keeping newer work.

scenes.name: import-inputs
scenes.text: For the next import, bring today's CSV export and the update you plan to import. Choose what should change. Here, I want prices to change, with a maximum increase or decrease of twenty-five percent. Payment statuses should stay as they are.

scenes.name: import-held-changes
scenes.text: Rewind finds twenty-two ordinary price updates. It holds out a price multiplied by one hundred, a blank price, and twenty-four unwanted payment changes. The unknown record ID stays out too. I can remove any other update before approving.

scenes.name: import-exact-approval
scenes.text: I review the exact twenty-two cells. Approval is tied to both files, my chosen rules and the exact selection. Changing any of those requires a new plan. The import updates existing records by ID and preserves other fields.

scenes.name: import-execution
scenes.text: Rewind builds the approved CSV inside gVisor on Vultr, then executes that import against a disposable copy. Fresh workers inspect both outputs. The controller independently checks every approved and protected value. This recurring check makes no model calls.

scenes.name: import-result-downloads
scenes.text: The import is checked and ready. All twenty-four records and their payment statuses remain. I download the approved import and resulting export, with a complete change list. If the business data changes before importing, I check again against a fresh export.

scenes.name: recovery-versions
scenes.text: When an import has already gone wrong, I bring three versions: the last good copy, a checkpoint just after the mistake, and today's file. The checkpoint helps identify the later edits that should stay. CSV and SQLite are supported.

scenes.name: ai-investigation
scenes.text: I describe the mistake: prices were multiplied by one hundred. Vultr Serverless Inference writes diagnostic code that actually compares the copies in its own gVisor environment. The controller checks the proposed repair against separate trusted inspections, rather than trusting the agent's description.

scenes.name: recovery-approval
scenes.text: The agent proposes restoring one hundred seventeen prices. Three prices changed again afterward, so they are protected. I review and approve the exact repair. A whole-backup replacement would lose newer invoices and updates. Rewind keeps today's records and every value outside my approval.

scenes.name: ai-recovery
scenes.text: A second Vultr call writes the repair. It runs on copies in another isolated container, without network access or controller credentials. A fresh trusted worker reads the output. The controller checks the resulting values independently. The agent cannot mark its own repair as passed.

scenes.name: recovery-result
scenes.text: One hundred seventeen prices are restored. All one hundred twenty-seven invoices remain, including seven newer records, twenty payment updates and three later price edits. The replacements match the good version. Every other cell keeps today's value.

scenes.name: recovery-downloads
scenes.text: I download the recovered CSV and all one hundred seventeen changes. Every data check passed, the originals stayed unchanged, and all seven temporary containers were removed before download became available. You get a checked copy to review and apply.

scenes.name: vultr-containment
scenes.text: This separate containment test also ran on Vultr. A program tries to keep running. Rewind stops it at the two-second deadline and confirms removal. The broader checks also reject whole-backup replacements and unchecked imports. All fifty-five test containers were removed.

scenes.name: why-a-team-would-pay
scenes.text: Why would a business pay? Someone has to check each supplier price list or finance import, and clean up mistakes afterward. Rewind helps that person review routine updates and recover precise errors while keeping newer work. That is a recurring job with a clear reason to come back.
